tasks.notes: plan-defect: the two patch cuts are captured through `execSeam`'s UTF-8 stdout string and written with `fs.writeFileSync` (fleet/publish-fold.mjs:416-417), so a path git treats as TEXT but whose content is not valid UTF-8 (e.g. a latin-1 source file — `--binary` only base64-encodes paths git calls BINARY) reaches `main.patch`/`run.patch` with U+FFFD substitutions. The kernel's `git apply` then fails on the mangled hunk and the fold degrades to `cannot fold`. The engine's own capture avoids this by never routing a diff through a string: `fleet/run-waves.mjs:330` passes `--output=<file>` and lets git write the bytes. The fix cannot land inside this diff: M2 pins the cut as `git diff --binary --full-index --no-renames <BASE>..<TIP>` — "that argv" — and the exam pins it exactly (`assert.deepEqual(diffs.slice(0, 2), [...])`, fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs leg (a.1)), so adding `--output=` would diverge from both. Settling this needs M2's argv clause relaxed to permit `--output=`, after which fleet/publish-fold.mjs:416-417 and the leg (a.1) deepEqual would both change. Not blocking: no clause requires non-UTF-8 text safety, the exam is green, and the failure mode is a refusal rather than a silently wrong candidate.; The global constraint "No token in any argv: the folder reads its credentials from the environment the unit hands it and sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to the run tree's `claude/` for the worker it composes" carries no `Check:`, and I read it as requiring the composed worker env to carry `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = <run dir>/claude` with no credential on any command line. The diff meets it by inspection — fleet/publish-fold.mjs:278-285 builds `env: { ...process.env, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: path.join(runDir, 'claude'), ... }` and no argv anywhere in the module carries a token — but no leg asserts it, even though the exam's own stub already captures exactly the data needed: `stubAgent` records `sink.composedWith = composeOpts` (fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs, the `stubAgent` helper) and nothing ever reads it, leaving that recording as dead fixture code. Adding one assertion in leg (d), where a resolver is actually dispatched, would both retire the dead capture and pin the constraint.; fleet/publish-fold.mjs:540 — on `resolveConflicts` returning `ok: false`, the receipt's `path` is taken from the LAST transcript (`(last && last.path) || open[0].path`), but Context specifies `path` = "the first outstanding conflict's path". These agree for every shape M5 names (BLOCKED and the twice-rejected reply both push a transcript for the conflict being worked before parking), so no exam leg is affected. They diverge in one reachable corner: on a multi-conflict wave where conflict 1 resolves and the dispatch for conflict 2 throws, `resolveConflicts` parks without pushing a transcript for conflict 2, so the receipt would name conflict 1's path. Consider recording the parked path from the reason/outstanding position rather than the last transcript, or documenting the approximation.; fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs:340 — `stubAgent` records `sink.composedWith = composeOpts` but no assertion ever reads it, so the capture is dead scaffolding. It is also the natural place to cover the global constraint "No token in any argv: the folder … sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to the run tree's `claude/`": that constraint carries no `Check:` command and is currently evidenced only by the code line (fleet/publish-fold.mjs:274-286, the `env` block handed to `composeAgent`), not by any test. Suggested: in leg (d), assert `stub.composedWith.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR === path.join(fx.runDir, 'claude')` and that no `composedWith` argv/env value carries a token.; unverified: the exam evidence settles `node fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs` exiting 0 standalone, but not that it fits the committed suite's own budget — `tests/test_fleet_suite.py:44` runs each `fleet/tests/test_*.mjs` under a 120 s `subprocess.run(..., timeout=120)`, and this sim builds ~20 per-case fixtures (each a template copy plus a `provisionRunTree` local clone) while driving the real `fold_wave.py` and `compile_plan.py`. The plan's mitigation (build the seeded origin and clones once, copy per case) is implemented at fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs:134-183. What would settle it: the wall time of one `pytest tests/test_fleet_suite.py -k test_publish_fold` run on the sim host, under `--dist load` contention.

deferredVerification.deliverable: fleet/publish-fold.mjs — the resolver dispatch against the real `claude` CLI (the `conflict parked` on BLOCKED, the twice-rejected reply, and the resolved fold)
deferredVerification.why: As Context records, the CLI has no injection seam for a stub resolver, so every resolver-driven shape is asserted in-process with a stub `deps.makeAgent`. The real path — `composeAgent` -> `createRunWorker` -> the `claude` binary answering `RESOLVER_SCHEMA` under the confine hook — needs a live model and credentials and is never executed by the committed suite. The composition itself is structurally correct (labels route to the read-only `resolver` role via `roleForLabel`, cwd to `clones/integration` via `makeCwdFor`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to the run tree's `claude/`), but its behaviour is unexercised here.

deferredVerification.deliverable: The plan's elicited Claim end to end — two concurrent plans touching one file both merging on their own, no 405 and no hand rebase, with the second run's evidence showing its fold onto main
deferredVerification.why: The folder is the last missing piece and its own Claim (fold onto main's tip at publish) is met in the tree, but the surrounding half is the boot script's: the `fleet-fold-<N>-<attempt>` systemd unit, `push_head`'s `--force-with-lease`, the merge PUT, the 405 retry into attempt 2, and the evidence push to the target. Those need a real GitHub target, a sandbox VM and an actual cross-run race. The plan itself states #715 closes only when its Tier-2 metric is met on live runs, so this is deferred rather than a shortfall.
